title: Uptime field journal: 50-day experiments for cross-team reliability
content:
Summary:
This is a working field journal for a 50-day, cross-functional set of experiments to validate operational controls, SLO gating heuristics, and rapid rollback behavior across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. The doc is intentionally tactical — notes, hypotheses, brief experiment logs, and decisions to seed a formal runbook after the 50-day run.

Context & why now:
- Recent customer incidents highlighted unpredictable tail latency and noisy throughput spikes during model rollouts.
- We need rapid, observable controls that product teams can apply without deep infra changes (tempo-based SLO gating + lightweight error-budget allocations).
- The goal: reduce user-facing time-to-degrade and mean-time-to-recover while keeping unit cost within target.

Primary objectives (measurable):
1) Validate a three-tier SLO gating policy (fast-fail, guarded-rollout, full-rollout) across 3 service classes within 50 days.
   - Success: 95% of gated rollouts that hit error-budget-triggered fallbacks recover to steady-state within 20m with automated routing fallback.
2) Surface high-fidelity signals for tail latency (p99.9, 99.99 where applicable) in the Redwood Console and reduce false positives by 40%.
3) Prove an error-budget micro-allocation pattern for feature teams (<=2% of global error budget per team/month) with live enforcement using rate-limited tokens.

Hypotheses to test:
- H1: Prefix/KV cache warm-up reduces p99.9 for common prompt families by >=30% within first 5 tokens.
- H2: Deploying a lightweight canary router (route=80% stable, 20% canary with KV warmup window) will detect quality regressions without increasing global error budget burn rate by >15%.
- H3: Tempo-based SLO gating (time-windowed error-rate tolerance) will be more permissive for spikey but short-lived load patterns, reducing unnecessary rollbacks.

Experiment matrix (high-level):
- Week 0 (prep): instrumentation checks, dashboard smoke-tests, create experiment feature flags, announce calendar and Slack channel (#sre-uptime-canvas).
- Weeks 1-2: Prefix cache experiments on dedicated pools for two high-traffic services. Metrics: p50/p95/p99/p99.9, cache hit ratio, token cost delta. Tickets: SRE-4321 (cache & agent), PLAT-1203 (dedicated pool config).
- Weeks 3-4: Canary routing + slow-roll experiment across hosted API paths; introduce tempo SLO gating at canary level. Observe error-budget consumption.
- Weeks 5-6: Error-budget micro-allocations for three product teams; simulate noisy third-party dependencies with chaos tests in staging.
- Continuous: Incident drills and runbook rehearsals every second Tuesday; compile decision log at end of each week.

Roles, RACI and communication ritual:
- Lead (owner): Priya Nair — experiment coordination, stakeholder updates.
- Engineering leads: Chen Li (serving-runtime), Alex Gomez (platform routing), Maya Patel (observability).
- Product liaison: Tomás Alvarez — product acceptance criteria, customer impact mapping.
- RACI:
  - Decide: Priya Nair + Chen Li (go/no-go on rollouts)
  - Responsible: service/feature engineers
  - Consulted: SRE, platform, product
  - Informed: GTM and customer success for major rollback events
- Daily stand: 15-min async updates in Slack; weekly 30-min sync on Fridays for decision capture.

Metrics and dashboards (what to watch):
- SLO coverage: % of routes covered by tempo gating and whether policy applied successfully.
- Error budget burn rate: per-team and global (1h/24h windows).
- Latency tails: p99.9 and p99.99 histogram buckets; correlate with model size and seq-len.
- Cost signals: tokens-per-response and 95th percentile GPU GPU-time-per-request.
- Observability health: % alerts that are actionable vs noise. Goal: reduce noise by 40%.

Quick dashboard checklist (observability owners should confirm):
- Synthetic probes representing three customer personas.
- Cold-start vs warm-start KPI split (KV-prefix warm cache vs cold).
- Error budget burn widget by team + linked drilldowns.
- Canary health timeline with request traces aggregated to sample level.

Runbooks & guardrails (draft):
- Automated fallback policy (Tiered):
  - If p99.9 > threshold for T minutes AND error budget burn > X% over last Y minutes -> trigger route fallback to smaller model variant and enable KV prefetch.
  - If fallback occurs: automated P0 page to oncall + create ephemeral incident channel.
- Manual rollback criteria: repeated quality/regression signals across two independent monitors (traces and user-facing error-rate) for >15m.
- Canary abort steps: immediate rollback of canary routing and freeze of further canaries across region for 30m.

Risks, unknowns and mitigation ideas:
- Risk: False-positive tail spikes caused by synthetic tests that don’t match production traffic.
  - Mitigation: Re-weight synthetic probes and incorporate real user sampling.
- Risk: Cross-team contention for limited dedicated pool capacity during parallel experiments.
  - Mitigation: Reserve small burst pools and schedule experiments with explicit runway windows.
- Unknown: Impact of quantization knobs on latency vs QA for low-cost variants.
  - Plan: Run small A/B with QA promptset and human review for initial experiments.

Decision log snapshot (examples):
- 2026-10-15: Decided to use tempo-based gating prototype v1 (window=5m, tolerance=1.5x baseline error) instead of strict rate-based gating. Rationale: observed short spikes during model warmups.
- 2026-10-22: Opted to run prefix cache experiment on dedicated pools only to avoid skewing hosted billing metrics.

Weekly note template (for quick capture):
- Week #: lead, short objective, what we ran, primary signals, anomaly notes, next actions.

Deliverables by day-50:
- Final experiment report with decision log and recommended SLO gating config for GA.
- A compact runbook (<=2 pages) for rollout-time fallbacks and canary abort checklist.
- Dashboard templates and a small set of alerts with tuned thresholds (owner: observability).
- Draft RFC for error-budget micro-allocation model and allocation UI in Redwood Console.

Next immediate actions (today):
1) Create SRE-4321 and PLAT-1203 tickets (done, link above).
2) Notify product teams with proposed micro-allocation percentages and ask for acceptance within 48h.
3) Spin up a dedicated pool with a tiny burst reserve and share access to experiment leads.
4) Create a short run of synthetic probes that mirror three user personas and validate they surface in the console.

Notes to self (working):
- Keep logs terse here — this doc will be copied into confluence and turned into a stable runbook after day-50.
- Avoid over-automating fallbacks until we have solid canary signal coverage.

Appendix: quick checklist for engineers starting an experiment
- Confirm feature flag exists and is scoped to non-prod first.
- Confirm observability tags and spans include experiment_id and team_id.
- Add a discovery/expectations comment to PRs that affect latency or routing.
- Run chaos job in staging and confirm rollback works in <5m.

End of field journal (live updates will be appended as the experiment progresses).
